featured_reviews.name: Kisankumar Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari is located in Goregaon and in common language known as Mumbai Film City.
Many popular movies are shot here including the recently released blockbuster Dhurandhar - the climax scene where hamza is in the car was shot in this film city.

The place is amazing and here they offer tour of the entire city within 2 hours with an amazing bollywood show, 8d show which has immersive experience and various places to take photos and experience filmmaking process.

If you are travelling with family or friends you'll have a good time.

review_photos.caption: Entrance of film city
The famous temple which was a part of many iconic films

featured_reviews.name: pawan parihar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing experience visiting Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari (Film City), Mumbai. 🎬✨
It was exciting to see the real world of Bollywood, huge shooting sets, and beautiful locations surrounded by greenery. The atmosphere feels truly cinematic, and if you’re lucky, you may even spot live shooting or famous actors.
A must-visit place for movie lovers and anyone visiting Mumbai! 🌿🎥

featured_reviews.name: Abhishek Jha
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s very underwhelming. Rupees 1200 for this does not makes sense. I wanted to leave after the first experience but you can’t because there is no way other than their bus which will only take you after your complete trip. After 3.5 hours of wasting my time, I returned with a headache and 1200 less in my wallet.

2 stars because it atleast shows you a few shooting spot. And you should return just after the bus tour through the park.

The management also pays commission to auto and taxi guys and hence they take you there and make up stories about how awesome it is.

featured_reviews.name: Minakshi Puzari
featured_reviews.review_text: They take you on 1 hour bus ride through the location but you can't enter any set. You can only hope to see outdoor shooting. Impossible to see the superstars. Then they have 2 hour show which is average. Good for one time visit and only if you have nothing else to do

featured_reviews.name: darshan rawal
featured_reviews.review_text:
It is a fantastic place for shootings, it may be ads, webseries, daily soaps, movies, album songs, vertical series, etc, etc, etc

Anything you can imagine , you are welcomed to shoot here. For better transportation goverment bus service is available. Also a new flyover bridge is under construction from Oberoi mall to directly film city for avoiding the traffic and the transportation of shooting vehicles and equipments.

featured_reviews.name: Arpit Porwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bollywood Park is a decent place to visit, but not as grand as expected. Most of the film sets are either covered or not accessible, so you only get a glimpse of a few memorable spots like Taarak Mehta ka Ooltah Chasmah sets from far that are ok for quick photos.

The museum section is actually nice for clicking pictures, with well-designed setups and film-themed decor. The live show was the highlight well performed and quite engaging. Overall, it’s good for a one-time visit, especially if you enjoy Bollywood vibes, but don’t go in expecting full studio-style access as ticket price does not justify it.

featured_reviews.name: Mesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
HIGHLIGHT - If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

My recent visit to Mumbai Film City was far from what I had hoped. To start, the nearest metro station is Aarey, it is about 4 km away. From there, take an auto (no more than ₹150) straight to the official ticket counter. Be cautious, several individuals may try to sell you tickets along the way at inflated prices. Avoid them, as they are scammers.

After a long wait, we were taken inside the premises by an AC bus. Unfortunately, the experience was underwhelming from the beginning. Compared to Hyderabad's Film City, this one feels small, restricted, and poorly organized. Most of what you see are large tin sheets covering the sets, there is no access to the actual sets themselves. It felt like being shown billboards of what you could see, but never actually do.

The tour ends at Bollywood Park, which hosts a few staged performances. This was the only mildly enjoyable part. The on site restaurant is strictly vegetarian, which may not appeal to everyone, and the food was overpriced for its quality.

Overall, Mumbai Film City lacks substance, feels commercialized, and fails to deliver the behind the scenes magic one would expect. If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

featured_reviews.name: The lonely Traveller
featured_reviews.review_text: The official photo studio for years for the most famous reality show Koun Banega Corepati hosted my Amitabh Bachan. Stricts rules are followed here. Once you reach then make sure that the barcode received and you have got a print tag. If unable to get the barcode then one staff members will be there to help. Make sure that you have registered before. After print tag is received you can proceed for breakfast which is provided by the production house. Later you will have to hand over all digital watch, phones, wallets or any item like purse or you have carried. Can carry numbered spectacles. Also can carry items on which autograph is needed. Personal belongings have to be kept in bag and it's be monitored and kept safely and make sure to collect your token for same. Items on which autograph is needed will be collected by staff after show and can be collected at audience waiting area. There is canteen inside the premises so can sit and order and have food there. Ample parking spaces for cabs or traveling in private car. Was a fun visit to be on show.

featured_reviews.review_text: I had a fantastic time on the behind-the-scenes tour of a Bollywood set! It was amazing to see the practical aspects of filmmaking and the teamwork that brings movies to life. Tip: Don’t forget to ask questions—everyone is eager to share their experiences and insights!

review_photos.caption: 🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Bollywood films often shoot in various locations, from the vibrant streets of Mumbai to scenic rural landscapes across India.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Behind-the-scenes, the set is a bustling environment filled with crew members, including cinematographers, sound technicians, and makeup artists.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Bollywood, the Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai, is one of the largest and most prolific film industries in the world.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Many Bollywood films promote messages of love, family values, and social issues, resonating deeply with Indian audiences.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The popularity of Bollywood extends beyond India, with a large fan base in countries like the USA, UK, Canada, and several parts of Africa and the Middle East.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Bollywood films are known for their colorful song and dance sequences, often featuring elaborate choreography and vibrant costumes.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The production process can be complex, often requiring multiple takes to capture the perfect scene and ensuring high-quality results.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Editing is done after filming, where editors piece together footage to create a cohesive narrative and enhance the film’s pace.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Bollywood often celebrates cultural festivals and events, incorporating them into the storyline, showcasing the richness of Indian traditions.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - A typical Bollywood film can have a runtime of anywhere from 90 minutes to over three hours, with many incorporating an intermission.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The industry produces over 1,500 films annually, showcasing a wide range of genres, including romance, drama, action, and comedy.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Filmmakers often conduct extensive location scouting to find the perfect backdrop for key scenes, which adds authenticity to the film.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The director plays a pivotal role in guiding the artistic vision of the film, collaborating closely with actors and crew throughout the process.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The art department is responsible for sourcing props and decorations that align with the film’s theme, ensuring authenticity and creativity.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The main actors, known as “stars,” are often celebrated as cultural icons and can command significant influence over their fans.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - A behind-the-scenes tour of a Bollywood set reveals the hard work and passion of countless individuals, all dedicated to bringing cinematic stories to life.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - Set designers play a crucial role in creating the visual aesthetic of the film, often constructing elaborate sets that enhance the story’s narrative.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The term “Bollywood” is a portmanteau of “Bombay” (the former name of Mumbai) and “Hollywood,” reflecting its cinematic aspirations.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India - The music of Bollywood films is an essential element, often released as soundtracks before the film’s premiere and contributing to its marketing.
🇮🇳 Mumbai, India -  Wardrobe departments meticulously design and curate costumes that reflect characters’ personalities and the film’s cultural context.

featured_reviews.name: Indiana Jonas
featured_reviews.review_text:
We joined this tour expecting a true immersion into the world of Bollywood.
The studio is indeed a real working studio used for filming, but the experience offered does not quite match what one might imagine from a “Bollywood tour.”

You get to see sets and filming areas, but it is not access to major film productions or the behind-the-scenes world of iconic Bollywood movies. The visit feels more like a tourist-oriented presentation than an authentic insight into the Indian film industry.

It is not a bad visit in itself, but it may create expectations that are not fully aligned with reality. In my view, it is not truly a Bollywood experience in the way it is advertised.

name: Chandivali Studio
description: Chandivali “Studio,” As It Is Known, Began Its Journey In 1940 When Chandrarao Kadam Purchased A Large Parcel Of Land At Chandivali, Near Powai Lake In Mumbai, India. His Idea Was To Create Multiple And Diverse Filming Locations In One Place, Use Them For Shooting His Own Films But Also Make These Locations Available To Other Film Producers. This Innovative Concept Was Unprecedented In The Indian Movie Industry And Became A Template That Many Others Would Follow. It Took Mr. Kadam Nearly Four Years To Clear And Level The Existing Forestland And A Lifetime To Create And Develop The Parcel’s Various Themed Areas. Chandivali Outdoor Location Opened For Business In 1944.

featured_reviews.review_text: Entrance fees are almost USD40. There is nothing to see. You see the studios and set from the outside. Most of the sets are in ramshackle condition. The entire place is little better than  a slum. You get to watch a show which consists of dance, singing and comedy. All are substandard productions!

featured_reviews.name: Shehzad Nur Tayus
featured_reviews.review_text: Nice place. A tourist bus will support to show around with a guide. Can see different shooting spot, structure used in different movies and dramas.

featured_reviews.name: Imran Khan
featured_reviews.review_text: This is the most beautiful shooting location in—Chitranagri (Mumbai Film City)—and my favorite spot. Love you! ❤️😘

featured_reviews.name: Bhanita Das
featured_reviews.review_text: The place is large, have things to see, but they are charging way more for these. ₹ 1100  per head is too much for a place like this.

featured_reviews.name: Eliza Vu
featured_reviews.review_text: The museum charged foreign tourists almost 40 dollars/ head. However, the service is really bad. Most of your guides spoke Hindi and translated very little content into English. In addition, when I requested English translation, two tour guided provided very superficial rendering of information. It is not worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Sarah F
featured_reviews.review_text: Worst experience ever and a big scam! Do not waste your time here, the tour bus takes you through the jungle with one or two tents up and tells you that there is a shooting happening here but you don’t see anything or anyone. Then after 20 minutes of driving through the jungle they take you to an indoor place with one little stage where a junior artist performs a comedy show. There’s also an overcrowded cafe there with little stirring area. You are charged 3000 rupees as a tourist for a worthless experience.

featured_reviews.name: Suyojit Choure
featured_reviews.review_text: say in one sentence.  Please don't waste your money and time in watching Film City.  Because after returning from there you will have nothing but regret.  Now read further to know why I am saying this.  You will be charged a ticket of more than thousand rupees in Film City and you will see nothing except old ruins.  If you are going thinking that you will get to see any hero or see the shooting of any film, then it is your mistake.  If you want to see your favorite hero, then find out his house and visit his house, but do not waste money in Film City.  Here only you are fooled.  We 4 people went to see, we were charged about 4500 rupees.  While the one we got to roam there was worth less than 1500 rupees.
